'''Carolina Bhering de Araujo''' (born in 1976) is a Brazilian mathematician specializing in [[algebraic geometry]], including [[birational geometry]], [[Fano variety|Fano varieties]], and [[foliation]]s.{{r|words|escavador|ewm|mgp|urca}} Other than her research in mathematics, she is also known for her efforts for improving the conditions for women mathematicians.

== Education and career ==
Araujo was born and raised in [[Rio de Janeiro]], [[Brazil]].{{r|quanta}} She did her undergraduate studies in Brazil, completing a degree in mathematics in 1998 from the [[Pontifical Catholic University of Rio de Janeiro]].{{r|escavador}} She earned her PhD in 2004 at [[Princeton University]], where her dissertation, supervised by [[János Kollár]], was titled ''The Variety of Tangents to Rational Curves''.{{r|ewm|mgp|quanta}}

She is currently a researcher at the [[Instituto Nacional de Matemática Pura e Aplicada]] in Brazil (IMPA), and the only woman (as of 2018) on the permanent research staff at IMPA.{{r|words}} She is also a Simons Associate at the [[International Centre for Theoretical Physics|Abdus Salam International Centre for Theoretical Physics (ICTP)]]. She is the vice-president of the Committee for Women in Mathematics at the [[International Mathematical Union]].{{r|quanta}}

During and after her PhD, Araujo developed techniques related to Japanese mathematician [[Shigefumi Mori]]'s proposed theory of [[Algebraic_curve#Rational_curves|rational curve]]s of minimal degree, which she published in 2008.{{r|quanta}}{{ran|A}}

== Recognition ==

Araujo won the L'Oreal Award for Women in Science in Brazil in 2008.{{r|urca|loreal}}

Araujo was both an organizer and an invited speaker at the 2018 [[International Congress of Mathematicians]].{{r|ewm|quanta}} She led the inaugural World Meeting for Women in Mathematics (WM)<sup>2</sup> in August 2018.{{r|quanta}} She was also one of the female mathematicians profiled in the short documentary called ''Journeys of Women in Mathematics'', funded by the [[Simons Foundation]].{{r|words|quanta|journeys}}

Araujo was awarded the 2020 [[ICTP Ramanujan Prize|Ramanujan Prize]] from the [[International Centre for Theoretical Physics]].{{r|ramanujan}}

She is included in a deck of playing cards featuring notable women mathematicians published by the [[Association of Women in Mathematics]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Mathematicians of EvenQuads Deck 1 |url=https://awm-math.org/publications/playing-cards/deck1/#araujo |access-date=2022-06-18 |website=awm-math.org}}</ref>
